Empirical M formula by Then et al. (2015) with uncertainty

Source: R/MstochThen.R
MstochThen.Rd

Estimates the natural mortality rate (M) for each resample of a bootstrapped growth analysis with the growth-based estimator of Then et al. (2015) ("Then_growth" in M_empirical), including the uncertainty of the estimator itself: for each resample, the model of Then et al. (2015) with coefficients from a bootstrap of their data is used for each resample.

Usage

MstochThen(boot, resid = FALSE, seed = NULL, CI = 95)

Arguments

boot

an object of class `lfqBoot` with bootstrapped growth parameters (e.g. from ELEFAN_GA_boot)

resid

logical; should the residual error of the model of Then et al. (2015) be included (Default: `FALSE`)? See details.

seed

optional; seed for the random numbers. Resample `x` uses `set.seed(seed + x)`. Default (`NULL`): the seeds of the resamples in `boot$seed`.

CI

percentage for confidence intervals (Default: 95)

Value

The lfqBoot object with the additional column M_Then (in bootRaw, maxDen, median and CI).

Details

The model \(M = a K^b L_\infty^c\) of Then et al. (2015) was refitted (with nls) to 2000 bootstrap samples of their data of 230 stocks. The data themselves are not included in TropFishR, only the resulting 2000 sets of coefficients and the residuals of the fit to all data. For each resample, one of the coefficient sets is selected at random and M is predicted with the growth parameters of the resample. This accounts for the uncertainty of the estimated coefficients (i.e. of the mean M of species with the given growth parameters). With `resid = TRUE`, the scatter of individual species around the model is included as well: the prediction is multiplied with a randomly selected residual of the fit to all data (on the log scale, \(M_{obs}/M_{fit}\)), which results in much wider confidence intervals. The results are reproducible, because each resample uses its own seed (see `seed`).

References

Then, A. Y., J. M. Hoenig, N. G. Hall, D. A. Hewitt. 2015. Evaluating the predictive performance of empirical estimators of natural mortality rate using information on over 200 fish species. ICES J. Mar. Sci. 72: 82-92.

Examples

data(alba_boot)
res <- MstochThen(alba_boot)
res$maxDen
#>       Linf          K   t_anchor       phiL     agemax     M_Then 
#> 10.0096156  2.7150279  0.4908732  2.4346091  2.0000000  3.1399201 
res$CI
#>         Linf        K  t_anchor     phiL agemax   M_Then
#> lo  9.171726 1.547109 0.2486596 2.114423      1 1.758586
#> up 11.478216 4.165708 0.5486528 2.739438      2 6.588096

## including the residual error of the model
res <- MstochThen(alba_boot, resid = TRUE)
res$CI
#>         Linf        K  t_anchor     phiL agemax     M_Then
#> lo  9.171726 1.547109 0.2486596 2.114423      1  0.4997372
#> up 11.478216 4.165708 0.5486528 2.739438      2 12.5964694
